source.title: GridMind R3: validate expert-reviewed, supplier-specific bill screening before any live engine
source.body:
## Objective
Validate a **bounded, permissioned industrial electricity bill screening method**, not a generic utility audit or autonomous AI savings calculator. This is GridMind's **R3 leading discovery hypothesis**, not the selected paid wedge. **No real factory data** in the public repo, demo or unapproved Supabase.

**Authority:** [sole Master Plan](https://github.com/vartmaansharma-blip/gridmind-insights-ea7a9796/blob/strategy/gridmind-3-1-resolution-first-2026-10-17/docs/gridmind-master-plan-2026-10-11.md), [sole buyer discovery tracker](https://github.com/vartmaansharma-blip/gridmind-insights-ea7a9796/blob/strategy/gridmind-3-1-resolution-first-2026-10-17/docs/gridmind-buyer-discovery-sprint-2026-10-11.md), [method contract](https://github.com/vartmaansharma-blip/gridmind-insights-ea7a9796/blob/strategy/gridmind-3-1-resolution-first-2026-10-17/docs/product/gridmind-r3-electricity-screening-method-and-test-fixtures-2026-10-18.md) and [competitor learning register](https://github.com/vartmaansharma-blip/gridmind-insights-ea7a9796/blob/strategy/gridmind-3-1-resolution-first-2026-10-17/docs/research/gridmind-industrial-intelligence-competitor-learnings-2026-10-18.md).
JSERC official [tariff-order index](https://jserc.org/tariff.aspx) lists distinct JBVNL, Tata Steel Limited, Tata Steel UISL and DVC cases, and their order periods.

## Deliverables and sequencing
- [ ] **Professional reviewer route:** Identify qualified industrial tariff/energy candidates, confirm individual competence, available reviewer cost and scope; do not claim contract or approval until actual agreement and appropriate adult/business authorization.
- [ ] **Supplier-specific source inventory:** JBVNL, TSL, TSUISL (plus other supplier if encountered), actual contract/category, dated FY order, effective period and applicable corrections; reviewer validates relevant line computations.
- [ ] **Paper/fictional method:** Exactly three initial screening questions: contract demand, PF where applicable, tariff category. Classify NO_OBVIOUS_ISSUE / MORE_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED / POTENTIAL_REVIEWABLE_EXPOSURE / OUT_OF_SCOPE. Never guarantee refunds or infer a PF fee universally.
- [ ] **Synthetic acceptance:** Represent all 12 scenarios in the method contract, including missing order/units, bill spanning revised rates, unqualified reviewer, withdrawn rights, stale approval, and tenant denial; show explicit expected result. No actual consumer IDs/bills in fixtures.
- [ ] **Review costs:** Time-box preliminary screening and account for *negative/unconverted* screens, sales time, expert fee and founder labor. Record only factual buyer results in the sole tracker.
- [ ] **R2 comparison:** Arrange substantive finance/commercial buyer research (R2) using a predeclared rubric. R3 does not win merely because it has a spreadsheet.
- [ ] **Security gate:** No production import, new schema/route/payment gateway or real processing until existing #29/#130 release, professional/contract and data-rights checks pass.
- [ ] **Evidence and milestone review:** At Nov 10 interim gate log actual progress, unresolved access issues and whether further screening is justified; any revised decision date must be explicitly recorded rather than silently assumed.

## Exclusions
No physical electrical work, automated machinery/grid control, live customer-data uploads, generalized energy auditing, guaranteed savings, broad ERP integration, digital twins, multi-domain product implementation, or changes to existing PR #136 release authority.

## Definition of done
A qualified domain reviewer has explicitly approved the narrow method; synthetic negative tests are demonstrably reproducible; costs and access are recorded honestly; customer-facing wording is reviewed; actual buyer evidence, if any, appears only in the current buyer tracker. **A documentation commit or passing CI is NOT completion.**

**Related existing work:** #40 (wedge), #39/#95 (access), #51 (independent review), #104 (evidence core), #29/#130 (production security). Current documentation belongs to existing draft PR #136.

comments.text:
## 18 Oct 2026 research checkpoint — delivery and regulatory boundaries

External checks support the **supplier-specific** design, but do not establish any customer exposure or potential savings: JSERC [tariff orders](https://jserc.org/tariff.aspx) list FY 2026–27 JBVNL, TSL and TSUISL separately. Source provenance must include retail supplier, applicable classification, period, dated order and amendments; missing source or application ambiguity => **MORE_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED**, never a computed refund recommendation. PF charges are conditional on the applicable order.

**Professional reviewer sourcing:** Use BEE's [accredited auditor directory](https://beeindia.gov.in/show_content.php?lang=1&level=2&lid=56&ls_id=203) to verify potential qualification **only**—registration/accreditation, relevant past tariff/billing experience and actual review scope must be confirmed independently with an appropriately authorized adult. Directory listing does not mean availability, endorsement or a contract.

**First feasible experiment:** 12 fictional rule/negative fixtures already documented; next actual gate is *professional method sign-off* + expert quote + evidence of owner willingness to pursue a specific past bill issue compared with their incumbent utility/adviser. Establish whether negative screens can be performed economically. Keep real bill imports, public uploads, calculated savings and production data changes blocked under #29/#130.

**Comparator:** Independent R2 and R1 discovery still required under #40; no default commercial R3 winner. No physical work, energized equipment inspection or automated utility control.
